title: World War II
description: Their words are real. Their group chats are imagined. World War II unfolds through authentic historical words, shifting alliances, political rivalries, and the quiet absurdities of a world at war.

title: World War I
description: An assassination becomes an ultimatum; an ultimatum becomes a world war. Europe discovers that adding everyone to a crisis does not make it easier to resolve.
speakers: My allies have my full support.
An entirely reasonable position. Mine do too.
The world must be made safe for democracy.
Excellent. Can someone first get us out of this group?
system: Austria-Hungary added everyone to Local Dispute

title: The American Civil War
description: A nation splits. Its leaders, abolitionists, generals, and dissenters struggle over slavery, union, and freedom—while everyone insists the other side started the thread.
speakers: A house divided against itself cannot stand.
Power concedes nothing without a demand.
I propose to fight it out on this line if it takes all summer.
I had hoped for a shorter conversation.
system: South Carolina left Union · Created a new group

title: The Cold War
description: A divided planet, two superpowers, too many missiles, and an astonishing amount of arguing in public while negotiating in private. Nobody wants to leave. Nobody dares to mute.
speakers: Then perhaps we can stop shouting across the planet.
system: Group description updated: Mutually Assured Destruction

title: The Space Race
description: Rockets, rivalries, impossible deadlines, and the race beyond Earth. The Cold War acquires a launchpad—and a group chat with absolutely no room for a typo.
speakers: We choose to go to the Moon.
That’s one small step for a man...
system: The Moon was pinned to Race to the Future

title: The Manhattan Project
description: Scientists, soldiers, classified messages, and the race to split the atom. A breakthrough of astonishing ingenuity creates a question no one can put back in its box.
speakers: I have a concern about uranium.
Can we discuss where this is going?

title: The Great Recession
description: The housing bubble bursts. Banks wobble. Confidence vanishes. The people charged with keeping the financial system standing discover that the group is far too big to fail quietly.
speakers: We may need a new plan.
system: Lehman Brothers was removed from Too Big to Fail

title: The Great Depression
description: The party on Wall Street ends; the consequences reach nearly everywhere. Confidence, policy, and desperation collide in the long aftermath of the crash.
speakers: Stock prices have reached what looks like a permanently high plateau.
That is a very tall plateau.
The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.

title: The Scientific Revolution
description: The universe receives an update. Copernicus, Galileo, Bacon, Kepler, and Newton challenge centuries of accepted thinking—and discover that the group admins are not pleased.
speakers: I looked. The Earth is moving.
I have three laws to propose.
I trust the acknowledgments are also governed by law.
system: Ptolemy lost admin privileges in Established Facts

title: The American Revolution
description: Thirteen colonies object to the terms of membership. Pamphlets, letters, arguments, and impossible choices lead to a declaration—and an entirely new group.
speakers: We hold these truths to be self-evident.
Then I suppose someone should organize this.
